item.title: Twenty names at State House: a crocodile rescue, the Chalala hero and the Trade Kings founder lead the Independence honours, with Kanyemba and the late Melu recognised for sport
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema decorated 20 people at an investiture ceremony at State House on Saturday 24 October, the 62nd anniversary of independence. The Times of Zambia's list runs from freedom fighters to a fisherman who pulled a colleague from a crocodile, Robby Chitambo, who helped police find 13 abducted young women in Chalala in 2022, and Trade Kings' Iqbal Patel. Copper Princesses coach Carol Kanyemba received the President's Insignia of Meritorious Achievement.

item.title: 'Not a mere procedural formality': M'membe says the 48-hour rule is being ignored after the August election, while Mweetwa tells the House the vote passed without violence
item.description: The Socialist Party used the Independence weekend to press two arguments. In a statement on Sunday 25 October, Fred M'membe said opposition figures and critics are being held beyond the constitutional 48 hours without charge, and called for it to stop. General secretary Cosmas Musumali called President Hichilema's COMESA role an opening for economic diplomacy but said he has not yet matured into an African leader. In Parliament, UPND's Cornelius Mweetwa said August saw no violence beyond the chaos after Brian Mundubile declared himself president-elect.

item.title: Home from a job that was not the job: two Zambian women repatriated from India over alleged exploitation, as Immigration removes 193 foreign nationals in a single day
item.description: The Department of Immigration said on Saturday 24 October that two Zambian women who went to India for work in July ended up in different work from what they had agreed, took refuge at the Zambian Embassy and were flown home, arriving at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on 15 October. The same statement reported the removal of 193 foreign nationals from Lusaka on Thursday 22 October, most of them Burundians, and a Zambian deported from Dubai. Spokesman Namati Nshinka urged job-seekers to verify agents and contracts before travelling.

item.title: Budget day is Friday: Musokotwane to present the 2027 estimates on 30 October, after which the House breaks for ten working days of sector scrutiny
item.description: Vice-President Mutale Nalumango told the National Assembly on Friday 23 October that Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane will present the 2027 National Budget on Friday 30 October, News Diggers reports. The Speaker will then suspend the business of the House for ten working days so that sector budgets can be analysed, with the House resuming on 24 November. The budget follows a K19.9 billion supplementary request dominated by maize payments, and a World Bank pledge to back the 2027 fiscal programme.

item.title: Two-thirds of the way: 675,459 farmers have redeemed their FISP inputs, and the Ministry tells agro-dealers to keep the shelves stocked as the El Niño advisories go out
item.description: The Ministry of Agriculture said on Saturday 24 October that 675,459 farmers had redeemed inputs under the 2026/27 Farmer Input Support Programme by 23 October, 65.93 per cent of the 1,024,434 targeted beneficiaries and ahead of the pace at the same point last year. Spokesman Balewa Zyuulu urged agro-dealers to keep enough stock to serve e-voucher holders without delay, told farmers to protect their redemption codes, and pointed them to official weather advisories as a possible El Niño season approaches.

item.title: Paid after death: the Auditor-General finds 77 deceased Ministry of Health workers were kept on the payroll for up to a year, at a cost of K5.79 million
item.description: The Auditor-General's report for 2025 says 77 health workers who had died remained on the Ministry of Health payroll for between one and twelve months, producing K5,790,691 in irregular payments, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. The same report found 63 officers past the retirement age of 60 still in service and paid K3.67 million, and 80 officers paid K1.16 million while unconfirmed in acting posts for up to 84 months. Who received the salaries of the dead is not stated.

item.title: 'Incompetently before the court': the Attorney-General says Mukandila should have appealed to the Minister before asking the High Court to restore his NRC and passport
item.description: The State has asked the Lusaka High Court to throw out Celestine Mukandila's application for judicial review of the Gazette notice that cancelled his national registration card and passport. Attorney-General Mulilo Kabesha argues that the Tonse Alliance secretary-general should first have appealed to the Minister of Home Affairs and that judicial review is no shortcut around a statutory appeal, Zambia Monitor and News Diggers report. Mukandila says the Act gives no power to cancel an NRC by Gazette notice, and that he had no notice, hearing or reasons.

item.title: Lumezi's council chairperson in custody: police detain NRPUP's Dawson Tembo over an alleged trespass and a damaged door, four days after the complaint was lodged
item.description: Police in Eastern Province have detained Dawson Tembo, the NRPUP chairperson of Lumezi Town Council, on allegations of trespass and malicious damage to property, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. A 20-year-old woman from a village under Chief Zumwanda complained on 19 October that he had entered her premises and damaged her door; police say he evaded arrest until Friday 23 October. He is expected in court and the allegations have not been tested; no response from Tembo or his party has been reported.

item.title: Nkana's run ends at Konkola: Blades win 2–0, Green Buffaloes come from behind in Kabwe and Chirundu win again, a day after Green Eagles dropped their first points
item.description: Week five of the MTN Super League transitional season closed on Sunday 25 October with Konkola Blades ending Nkana's three-match winning run 2–0 through Emmanuel Kunda and Idriss Ilunga Mbombo, Green Buffaloes beating Kabwe Warriors 2–1 away and Chirundu United winning 1–0 at Mufulira Wanderers, ZamFoot reports. On Saturday Green Eagles were held 0–0 by Nkwazi, their first dropped points, leaving Perry Mutapa's side top of Stream B on 10 points from four games.

item.title: 'I expected nothing less than victory': the Air Force commander meets Red Arrows at the airport, sets a CAF final as the next target and hands coach Chisi Mbewe a car
item.description: Red Arrows came home from Durban to a late-night reception at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport led by Zambia Air Force commander Lieutenant General Oscar Nyoni, who told the players their first CAF Confederation Cup group place should be the start of a push for the final, ZamFoot reports. Nyoni, the club's patron, presented head coach Chisi Mbewe with a Toyota Mark X, and FAZ's delegation leader Samuel Mwape called the qualification a milestone for Zambian football.

item.title: ‘Preserve this year’s stocks’: 1.25 million Zambians face hunger in the lean season as the Government activates its El Niño plan — but the Vice-President says the lights stay on
item.description: Two ministerial statements to Parliament on Friday 23 October set out what the 2026/27 El Niño season could mean. Vice-President Mutale Nalumango said about 1.25 million people in 93 districts could face acute food insecurity between August 2026 and March 2027 and that K31.7 million has already gone to the Disaster Risk Management Division; Green Economy Minister Gilbert Siame listed the ten driest districts and announced a US$3.6 million grant for weather stations. Asked about electricity, Nalumango said there would be no load-shedding.

item.title: ‘We do not break. We come together’: Hichilema’s message for Zambia at 62 — and the opposition’s answer that there is nothing yet to celebrate
item.description: Zambia marked 62 years of independence on Saturday 24 October under the theme ‘Our journey, our growth, our future’. In a message issued on the eve of the day, President Hakainde Hichilema paid tribute to the founding generation and set out his Grow Zambia Agenda; Tonse Alliance chairman Sakwiba Sikota told News Diggers he would ‘sadly’ commemorate rather than celebrate, and spoke of a ‘second independence’.

item.title: Three security zones for one constituency: the police lay out their plan for the Mandevu by-election on 5 November after the Tonse Alliance says its candidate was attacked
item.description: Inspector General of Police Graphael Musamba said on Saturday 24 October that Mandevu has been divided into three security zones with extra officers drawn from Lusaka Province, and that an alleged assault on Thursday 22 October will be investigated. The Tonse Alliance says FDD candidate Daniel Chisenga and other members were attacked by people in UPND regalia in Raphael Chota ward; the UPND had earlier challenged the alliance to name those it accuses.

item.title: ‘How do you ask “how did they apprehend?”’: the Vice-President tells MPs the Government will not explain Jay Jay Banda’s capture — and says the lean Cabinet is working
item.description: In Vice-President's Question Time on Friday 23 October, Mutale Nalumango said the Government would not account for the circumstances in which former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel Jay Banda was brought back from Mozambique and that Banda should explain himself. The Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report the exchange, which also covered FRA payments, COMESA and the size of the Cabinet.

item.title: US$122 million for Kalulushi: the ZDA signs a protection agreement with Rongxing to double a cathode plant, as the Mines PS says existing mines cannot deliver three million tonnes
item.description: The Zambia Development Agency signed an investment promotion and protection agreement on Thursday 22 October with Rongxing Investment, a Chinese-owned processor in Kalulushi that plans to lift copper-cathode capacity from 5,500 to 10,000 tonnes a year and add 194 jobs to its 506. At the Mining Insaka the same day, Permanent Secretary Hapenga Kabeta said the three-million-tonne target by 2031 depends on new projects, not expansion of what exists.

item.title: Out of Chimbokaila and back to court: Nakacinda’s ECZ summons trial is put off to 25 November after his lawyer says he is too ill, and the magistrate calls it the last adjournment
item.description: Raphael Nakacinda was due to open his defence on Friday 23 October to a charge of failing to comply with an Electoral Commission of Zambia summons in November 2022. His lawyer Nkula Bota told Magistrate Mbuywana Sinvula that he was unwell and needed medical attention, the Zambian Observer and News Diggers report; the case resumes on 25 November with a warning that no further adjournments will be granted.

item.title: History from twelve yards: Red Arrows lose 1–0 in Durban, level the tie and beat Kaizer Chiefs 3–2 on penalties to reach a CAF group stage for the first time
item.description: Bradley Cross's second-half header at Moses Mabhida Stadium on Friday 23 October cancelled out Alassane Diarra's first-leg goal in Ndola and sent the Confederation Cup tie to a shoot-out. Red Arrows won it 3–2, with Lebohang Maboe, Reeve Frosler and Ethan Chislett missing for Chiefs, and go into the 16-club group stage that begins in November — the first time the Zambia Air Force side has got that far.

item.title: Three games, three defeats, no points: Lea Motyka’s early goal gives France a 1–0 win and ends the Copper Princesses’ U-17 Women’s World Cup
item.description: Zambia's Under-17 women lost their final Group D match to France 1–0 in Morocco on Saturday 24 October, ZamFoot reports, after a 16th-minute goal by Lea Motyka from a Maelys Ane cross. Coach Carol Kanyemba had called the match ‘do or die’; the defeat follows the 5–0 loss to Japan and the 3–2 loss to Venezuela, and France go through to the round of 16.

item.title: Mpasela sinks the champions: MUZA beat Power Dynamos 1–0 to lead Stream A, Trident score six and ZESCO finally win in week five of the transitional Super League
item.description: Solomon Mpasela's 50th-minute goal gave FC MUZA a 1–0 win over defending champions Power Dynamos on Saturday 24 October and a three-point lead in Stream A, ZamFoot reports. Trident put six past Makeni All Stars, ZANACO beat Kansanshi 3–0, ZESCO United beat Mutondo Stars 5–0 for their first win of the season and Green Eagles stayed top of Stream B after a goalless draw with Nkwazi.

item.title: The bill for the bumper harvest: Musokotwane asks Parliament for K19.9 billion more, three-quarters of it to pay farmers for maize the FRA did not plan to buy
item.description: Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane presented Supplementary Estimates No. 2 of 2026 to the National Assembly on Thursday 22 October. Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer report that K14.7 billion of the K19.9 billion is owed to farmers who sold maize to the Food Reserve Agency, which bought 2.7 million tonnes against a target of 500,000, and that K18 billion of the total is to be raised by borrowing on the domestic market.

item.title: 121st on fundamental rights, 109th on corruption: Chapter One says the 2026 Rule of Law Index shows authoritarian habits ‘becoming entrenched’
item.description: The Chapter One Foundation says the World Justice Project's 2026 index places Zambia among countries with a five-year decline in at least one safeguard against authoritarian rule, Zambia Monitor and the Zambian Observer report. No government response to the index was reported, but in his maiden speech on Wednesday 21 October Monze East MP Jack Mwiimbu, until recently the Home Affairs minister, accused churches, civil society and the opposition of applauding those who abuse the President.

item.title: Same seven faces at State House: Hichilema re-appoints his advisers from Machila to Kayumba, while the Cabinet of his second term is still awaited
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema has re-appointed all seven members of his presidential advisory team, State House said in a statement on Thursday 22 October reported by Zambia Monitor and News Diggers. The re-appointments, under Article 92(2)(e) and (f) of the Constitution, retain officials who have served since 2021. They come in a week in which, News Diggers reports, UPND Alliance chairperson Charles Milupi was answering social-media claims that he would be left out of the Cabinet.

item.title: Second chair at the COMESA table: Hichilema becomes vice-chairperson as Mnangagwa takes over from Ruto in Harare and the bloc targets 15 per cent intra-regional trade
item.description: At the 25th COMESA Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare on Thursday 22 October, Zimbabwe's Emmerson Mnangagwa took the chair from Kenya's William Ruto and President Hakainde Hichilema was named vice-chairperson of the bloc's bureau, Lusaka Times, Kenya's Eastleigh Voice and Rwanda's KT Press report. The summit launched a 2026–2030 strategic plan that aims to lift trade among the 21 member states to 15 per cent of their total trade.

item.title: Cranes that run on road and rail: Japan signs a 999 million yen grant for Zambia Railways maintenance equipment, with the two sides quoting the dollar figure differently
item.description: Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane and Japan's ambassador Mikami Akiteru exchanged notes in Lusaka on Thursday 22 October for a grant to buy Japanese-made railway maintenance equipment, including crane-equipped motor cars and road-rail crane trucks, Lusaka Times and Zambia Monitor report. The ambassador put the grant at 999 million yen, about US$6.3 million; the Ministry of Finance's announcement gave US$6.17 million.

item.title: From the pit to the vault: ZCCM-IH tells London it will buy small-scale miners’ gold for the Bank of Zambia, citing a US$1.8 billion gap in the export data
item.description: ZCCM Investments Holdings chairperson Phesto Musonda told the Financial Times Africa Summit that the company's subsidiary Kyalo Goldfields will buy gold from licensed small-scale miners, pay them in kwacha and supply the metal to the Bank of Zambia, Zambia Monitor reports. He cited UAE records of nearly US$1.8 billion in gold imports from Zambia in 2023 against formal Zambian output of about 127,000 ounces last year — a discrepancy Africa Briefing traced in September to World Bank trade data.

item.title: ‘I was involved in bribing voters’: a former local-court magistrate turns petitioner’s witness in the Mwandi case, but says he has no evidence Iris Kaingu told him to do it
item.description: In the High Court sitting in Mongu, witnesses called by losing UPND candidate Sibeso Sefulo in her petition against independent Mwandi MP Iris Kaingu have admitted taking part in or receiving money during the August campaign, the Zambian Observer and News Diggers report. The former magistrate among them said he still supports Ms Kaingu and had no evidence she instructed any bribery; the judge warned the petitioner herself against interfering with a witness.

item.title: Thirty grammes and a famous name: the DEC says it has arrested rapper Chanda of ‘Chanda na Kay’ for alleged cannabis trafficking; he has not yet answered the claim
item.description: The Drug Enforcement Commission said in a statement on Thursday 22 October that it had arrested Edward Chanda, 28, the Lusaka rapper known as Chanda of the duo Chanda na Kay, for allegedly trafficking 30.3 grammes of dry loose cannabis, News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report. The arrest was announced alongside operations in Lusaka, Muchinga and Southern provinces. Mr Chanda has not yet appeared in court on the new allegation and his response has not been reported.

item.title: One goal to protect in Durban: Red Arrows meet Kaizer Chiefs at Moses Mabhida at 15:00 today with a Confederation Cup group place at stake
item.description: Red Arrows carry Alassane Diarra's 76th-minute winner from Ndola into the second leg of their CAF Confederation Cup second preliminary round tie against Kaizer Chiefs at Moses Mabhida Stadium in Durban on Friday 23 October, kick-off 15:00 Central African Time, ZamFoot reports. Coach Chisi Mbewe says his side is braced for an all-out Chiefs performance; assistant Kalililo Kakonje says the players know what is at stake.

item.title: Thirteen schoolboys in Baku: Zambia’s Under-15s open the first FIFA U-15 World Cup on Saturday in a group with Uruguay, Tanzania, Comoros, Moldova and Montserrat
item.description: Brian Kunsanama's 13-player squad, drawn largely from secondary and primary schools, left Lusaka on Tuesday 20 October for the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, which starts on Saturday 24 October, ZamFoot reports. Africa Top Sports places Zambia in Group X with Uruguay, Tanzania, Comoros, Moldova and Montserrat in a tournament played in an eight-a-side format.

item.title: Twelve months to the day: Raphael Nakacinda walks out of Chimbokaila after serving his defamation sentence, with a sedition count still to be ruled on in November
item.description: The Patriotic Front secretary general was released from Lusaka Central Correctional Facility on the morning of Wednesday 21 October, a year after he surrendered to begin an 18-month sentence for defaming President Hichilema. News Diggers and the Zambian Observer report that statutory remission cut the term to twelve months. Supporters in green carried him from the gates; a separate charge of seditious practices returns to the Lusaka Magistrates’ Court on 2 November.

item.title: A US$1.6 billion second act in Chilanga: Hichilema breaks ground on the UCF urea expansion and warns officials who slow projects that he will be ‘ruthless’
item.description: President Hichilema broke ground on Tuesday 20 October for the second phase of United Capital Fertilizer’s ammonia and urea plant in Chilanga, a US$1.6 billion expansion that the company and the President say will lift direct jobs from 7,400 to 10,000. He used the occasion to tell public officers that delays to investment approvals would not be tolerated in his second term.

item.title: ‘Not the rainfall of 1964’: a regulator tells the Insaka that Zambia’s tailings dams are not ready for three million tonnes of copper a year
item.description: At the Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka in Lusaka, the Minerals Regulation Commission’s inspections chief said tailings management standards remain inadequate and called for a national registry and independent engineering oversight. Konkola Copper Mines, meanwhile, told News Diggers it has spent US$500 million on its tailings leach plant with US$600 million more committed.

item.title: Posters, not practitioners: Lusaka’s mayor says his crackdown on illegal adverts is not aimed at traditional healers, after their association asks him to tread carefully
item.description: Mayor Chitambala Mwewa says Lusaka City Council will intensify the removal of unauthorised advertising on public infrastructure, including posters promising instant wealth, and that offenders face fines. Dr Rodwell Vongo of the Traditional Health Practitioners Association of Zambia has urged caution on spiritual matters while backing action against unregistered healers, Phoenix News reports.

item.title: 859 dead in three months: police count 12,865 road crashes between July and September, up 27 per cent on last year, as a head-on collision near Zimba kills two Americans
item.description: Zambia Police recorded 12,865 road traffic accidents and 859 deaths in the third quarter of 2026, against 10,126 crashes and 753 deaths in the same period of 2025, spokesperson Chipo Kaitisha said on Wednesday. Lusaka had almost half the crashes. The evening before, a Fortuner and a Hino collided on the Great North Road south of Zimba, killing two American passengers.

item.title: Drilling for a virus on the doorstep: Luapula tests its Ebola response with mobile laboratories as Nigeria becomes the fifth country with a case from the DRC outbreak
item.description: The Zambia National Public Health Institute ran a simulation in Milenge district this week to see how fast mobile laboratories can be deployed and return Ebola results, Zambia Monitor reports. The exercise comes as the World Health Organization confirms an imported case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in Abuja, Nigeria, with 44 contacts under watch, and as Kenya counts nine cases.

item.title: Two Public Procurement Act convictions in a week: Chongwe’s district health director fined K330,000 over contracts to his own company; a former Solwezi council officer jailed
item.description: Chongwe Resident Magistrate Francis Sato found Dr Mweene Nseluke guilty on ten counts of failing to declare a conflict of interest and fined him K330,000 on Monday 19 October, the Anti-Corruption Commission said in a statement reported by Zambia Monitor. News Diggers reports that the Solwezi Subordinate Court has separately jailed a former municipal council officer for three months over a K100,000 procurement.

item.title: Ahead twice, beaten in the 100th minute: the Copper Princesses lose 3–2 to Venezuela and go into Saturday’s match with France without a point
item.description: Elizabeth Mofya and Grace Phiri each put Zambia in front in Morocco on Wednesday night, but Venezuela equalised twice and Andrea Suárez scored the winner in the tenth minute of stoppage time — one of the latest goals in the tournament’s recent history. Zambia sit bottom of Group D on zero points and face France on Saturday 24 October. On Friday, Red Arrows defend a 1–0 lead against Kaizer Chiefs in Durban.

item.title: Thirty-two hours, 214 kilometres and the last lap alone: Cosmas Bwalya sets a Zambian record at the Backyard Ultra World Team Championship at York Farm
item.description: Cosmas Bwalya won Zambia’s leg of the 2026 Backyard Ultra World Team Championship at York Farm in Lusaka with 32 laps, or 214.6 km, beating the previous national best of 30 laps, News Diggers reports. Runner-up Alick Mashowo also passed the old mark with 31 laps, and Bwalya may now qualify for the 2027 individual world championship in Tennessee.

item.title: Forty years of NATAAZ: the national theatre festival gathers in Chingola, with a K100,000 grant per arts association and a nudge towards the digital stage
item.description: The National Theatre Arts Association of Zambia is holding its 2026 Senior Festival in Chingola as it marks its 40th anniversary, with the winners expected to feed the theatre nominations for the Ngoma Awards. A speech from the Ministry of Youth, Sport and Arts told performers to use digital platforms to reach audiences and funders, and said arts associations each received a K100,000 grant this year, Zambia Monitor reports.

item.title: Another week in Mukobeko: the State opposes bail for Mundubile and 17 others — and the hearing moves to 28 October with the DPP joined, the Zambian Observer reports
item.description: Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and 16 co-accused came back to the Lusaka High Court on Wednesday 21 October for the constitutional bail hearing that was adjourned on Monday. The State has now filed an affidavit opposing release, arguing that treason cases take time and that the Director of Public Prosecutions must be a party. The Zambian Observer reports that both sides agreed to join Gilbert Phiri and that the hearing now goes to 28 October. The 18 remain in custody in Kabwe.

item.title: One name, two sets of minutes: the Speaker recognises Ezra Tembo as Leader of the Opposition and ends the Kampyongo claim
item.description: Speaker Nelly Mutti told the National Assembly on Tuesday 20 October that she had received communication from the NRPUP’s secretary general confirming party president Ezra Tembo as Leader of the Opposition, with Milenge MP Gystave Chonde as Whip and Nyimba North MP Paul Lungu as Deputy Whip. The ruling closes a three-week dispute in which a rival caucus said it had elected Shiwang’andu MP Stephen Kampyongo to the post.

item.title: ‘A fugitive does not acquire immunity by crossing a border’: State House answers the civil-society groups questioning how Jay Jay Banda was brought home
item.description: A coalition of civil-society organisations has asked the Zambian and Mozambican governments to account for the cross-border apprehension of former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel ‘Jay Jay’ Banda and to explain how he came to be in a critical condition at Maina Soko Military Hospital. State House, through Clayson Hamasaka, calls the statement a political booby trap and says only bogus organisations could question the arrest of a man who, it says, publicly called for the President’s assassination.

item.title: K626 million in mining penalties never collected, K3.56 billion owed by the Ministry of Health: the Auditor-General’s account of 2025
item.description: The Auditor-General’s report on the accounts for the year to 31 December 2025, released by Acting Auditor-General Patricia Malaila, finds that the Ministry of Mines failed to collect K626.64 million in penalties from licence holders, that the Ministry of Health carries K3.56 billion in unpaid obligations some dating to 2014, and that only 27 of 5,595 confiscated mukula logs could be found. Unresolved findings fell from 33 to 27.

item.title: ‘Use it or lose it’, then a regional pitch: Botswana and the DRC bring proposals to the Mining Insaka after Hichilema’s warning to licence-holders
item.description: On the second day of the Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka at Mulungushi, Botswana’s minerals minister Bogolo Kenewendo and the DRC’s mines minister Louis Watum Kabamba urged shared processing, equipment manufacturing and border and rail cooperation, with a proposed Botswana–Zambia industrial campus tied to a 300 MW solar project. A day earlier President Hichilema told more than 1,300 delegates that tenements must be explored, that the state has spent almost US$100 million on a nationwide geophysical survey, and that the Insaka ‘is not a holiday’.

item.title: Every director sent home: the new ZEMA board orders a 60-day competency audit and installs an interim chief from UNZA
item.description: Green Economy and Environment Minister Gilbert Siame announced on Tuesday 20 October that the newly constituted board of the Zambia Environmental Management Agency has placed all of the agency’s directors on administrative leave pending assessments of competence and suitability, and appointed Dr Joel Kabika of the University of Zambia as interim director-general for six months. A policy institute has asked for due process and a clear line between the board and management.

item.title: Six days without a court date: Lima MP Kelvin Kaunda applies for bail from Mwembeshi after a transfer his lawyer says he was not told about
item.description: Kelvin Kaunda, the NRPUP MP for Lima, was arrested on 15 October on a charge of assault occasioning actual bodily harm over an incident during the August campaign. He has applied for bail, saying he has been held without being taken before a court; the Correctional Service confirms he has been moved from Lubwa police station to Mwembeshi remand, where his lawyer says he was refused access. His election petition hearing was adjourned on Tuesday because he was not in court.

item.title: A summit by video on Wednesday and one in Harare on Thursday: Hichilema’s two days of regional business, and the message he gave the Great Lakes
item.description: President Hichilema was due to join an extraordinary SADC summit held virtually on Wednesday 21 October to fill treaty positions and elect the next chair of the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security, Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe said, before travelling to Harare for the 25th COMESA summit on Thursday 22 October, where Zimbabwe takes the chair from Kenya. On Monday he told a Great Lakes ministerial meeting that hungry populations are hard to govern and that the region should trade food rather than post soldiers.

item.title: ‘A must-win for us’: the Copper Princesses face Venezuela in Rabat tonight after the 5–0 to Japan — and Ken Sekeletu keeps his belt in Tenerife
item.description: Zambia’s under-17 women play Venezuela at 20:00 CAT on Wednesday 21 October in their second Group D match at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, after losing 5–0 to Japan on the opening day. Both sides are without a point; coach Carol Kanyemba says one defeat is not the end of the tournament and captain Taonga Mubanga has promised a win. In Spain, Ken Sekeletu retained his featherweight title with a third-round stoppage.

item.title: From Matero to the launch stage: Olivia Tutu’s memoir ‘Authentic: A Life Chosen, Not Given’ is launched in Lusaka
item.description: Olivia Tutu, the 26-year-old founder of Youth on Sustainable Development, launched her ten-chapter memoir in Lusaka on Saturday 17 October, with Absa Bank chief executive Mizinga Melu as guest of honour and UNDP resident representative James Wakiaga among the speakers. The book was published in August and is expected on Amazon in January 2027.

item.title: ‘No jurisdiction’: Solwezi sends the Mundubile and Zulu sedition case to the High Court — and the question of a Lusaka hearing is left for the judges
item.description: Principal Resident Magistrate Mambwe Mukonde ruled on Tuesday 13 October that the Solwezi Magistrates’ Court cannot hear the two-count sedition case against Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, and referred it to the High Court. The State had not disputed the defence’s claim that the alleged offences took place in Lusaka. No High Court date has been set, the two men have still not taken plea, and the separate treason matter is untouched. In Lusaka, a bench warrant was issued for Binwell Mpundu in his own sedition case.

item.title: A scuffle on the Supreme Court steps: the Chief Justice tightens security after Davies Mwila is pushed to the ground — and the UPND condemns the attack while disputing the blame
item.description: Former PF secretary-general Davies Mwila was pushed to the ground outside the Supreme Court on Tuesday 13 October after a hearing in the Lima election petition. Chief Justice Mumba Malila called it an attack on the administration of justice and said security had been heightened. The UPND condemned the assault and dared a PF-Pamodzi youth official who blamed its cadres to produce evidence. Police have named no suspects.

item.title: A seat without a contest: Zambia joins the UN Human Rights Council for 2027–2029 — as Human Rights Watch calls the uncontested vote ‘a mockery’
item.description: The UN General Assembly elected Zambia to the 47-member Human Rights Council on Tuesday 13 October, alongside Ghana, Nigeria and Burundi for Africa. Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe called it a milestone and thanked the states that backed the bid. Every regional group had put forward exactly as many candidates as seats, for the second year running, and Human Rights Watch said that made the word ‘election’ a mockery.

item.title: The steepest fall in the region — and the heaviest interest bill: Moody’s on Zambia’s debt, as Musokotwane takes the case to Bangkok
item.description: Moody’s projects that Zambia and Ethiopia will record the largest reductions in government debt in sub-Saharan Africa, and lists Zambia among eight countries with a positive outlook — while also forecasting that about 35 percent of its revenue will go on interest in 2027, the heaviest burden in the region alongside Kenya. State House called the projection the result of ‘hard choices’. The Finance Minister is now at the IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok, where he spoke for African borrowers on Tuesday.

item.title: ‘Not reduced’: State House says CDF stays at K40 million and only the disbursements have changed — as the Treasury releases K806 million for schools
item.description: After the Finance Minister said next year’s Constituency Development Fund would fall below budget, State House said the allocation ‘has not been reduced and remains at 40 million kwacha per constituency’, with disbursements realigned to need and absorption. NRPUP’s Stephen Kampyongo says any cut will leave MPs unable to meet expectations the Government itself raised. Separately, the Treasury released K806.1 million in fourth-quarter school grants, completing more than K2.3 billion for 2026.

item.title: A truce over the tax ledger: ZRA halts penalties, certificate suspensions and debt recovery while migrated records are reconciled
item.description: After moving years of historical tax transactions from retired systems onto TaxOnline, the Zambia Revenue Authority says it will not impose penalties, suspend Tax Clearance Certificates or pursue debt recovery over unreconciled historical data while taxpayers check their accounts. Business associations had raised concerns about suspended certificates and the reliability of the migrated records. A technical working group has been set up; no end date for the reconciliation period has been given.

item.title: Back to their stations: the Ministry of Health sends 123 headquarters officers to their posts and orders a qualifications audit — as ZAMMSA starts hiring again
item.description: An internal assessment found 123 officers working at the Ministry of Health’s Lusaka headquarters under temporary arrangements, outside an approved establishment of 403 positions. Health Minister Roma Chilengi says they are being redirected to their substantive stations and that everyone left at headquarters will be assessed against professional benchmarks. ZAMMSA, whose entire workforce was dismissed, has advertised eight senior posts, and the Ministry says it is seeking cheaper financing for the sector.

item.title: ‘A matter concerning an individual’: the Government says clergy facing serious allegations should step aside — and the Green Party says the calls on Archbishop Banda are premature
item.description: Information Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana, in a statement that named no cleric, said it was advisable for clergy facing serious allegations to step aside while the facts are established, and that a case against an individual is not an attack on the Church. The statement follows the arrest of Lusaka Archbishop Alick Banda, who is contesting a charge in court. Two MPs say he should not preside at Mass meanwhile; Green Party leader Peter Sinkamba says resignation calls are premature and politically motivated.

item.title: Four goals and the road to Los Angeles reopens: the Copper Queens beat Uganda 4–1 in Ndola to go through 5–3 on aggregate — Ghana next, in February
item.description: Trailing 2–1 from Kampala, Zambia needed a performance at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium on Tuesday 13 October and produced one: Natasha Nanyangwe and Eneless Phiri scored inside 20 minutes, and Barbra Banda added two after the break for a 4–1 win and a 5–3 aggregate. Sylvia Kabene’s equaliser was Uganda’s only reply. The third round of the 2028 Olympic qualifiers brings Ghana, 10–0 aggregate winners over Mauritius, in February 2027.

item.title: A winning start in Rabat: Zambia’s futsal side beat Libya 3–1 at the Africa Cup of Nations — the hosts, Morocco, are next
item.description: Royd Chishala scored in the second minute and Patrick Mwila added two as Zambia opened their fourth Futsal Africa Cup of Nations with a 3–1 win over Libya in Rabat on Monday 12 October. Mohammed Abu Raas pulled one back late on. Andrea Cristoforetti’s side, who went out in the group stage in 2024, now face hosts Morocco on Wednesday 14 October and Algeria on Friday 16 October.

item.title: The bill for the maize: next year's CDF will be cut as the Treasury counts the cost of a bigger harvest
item.description: Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane says the 2027 Constituency Development Fund allocation will fall below what was initially budgeted, as the Treasury moves to contain this year's overspend — heavier-than-planned maize purchases chief among it. The Food Reserve Agency has been told to expect no Treasury money next season, and road funding is also under pressure.
